about: Engine notes of games built on the engine that this engine has resolved, matched by the note's topic and, where a note was named, by its id. node tools/egret.mjs notes reads a game's ENGINE-NOTES.md against it.

resolved.what: An embedded play (given a parent or a canvas) takes keys only while its canvas has the focus, so page buttons keep Tab, Space and Enter. A capture-phase listener that stops keys for play is no longer needed, and stops the game hearing keys.
With transparent: true the holder play makes for its canvas is clear, so the page shows under the canvas without clearing its background by hand.
The play guide says that game.canvas is the canvas play draws on, and that game.browser has no canvas of its own.
play takes pixelRatio, the render pixels per stage unit: a 1280 x 720 stage at 0.75 draws 960 x 540 pixels, with layout, input and semantic bounds still in stage units.

createAtlasLabel draws short labels on pages it shares with other such labels, and play's game.text uses it: a hundred labels on one screen take one of the 64 images a frame holds. getFrameUsage and onWarning tell the count before a frame is refused.
A label of play or of createAtlasLabel ends when its display, its parent or an ancestor is disposed, and gives back its raster.
chooseParagraphProvider gives CanvasKit where it loads and a canvas paragraph provider where it cannot, as in a WeChat mini game, with the same text geometry.
@egret/engine/web/wechat-text-input types into WeChat's own keyboard in a mini game.
In play, a sprite given to onTap, gestures or a drag source that has children and no hit area of its own is hit in its bounds, its children included.
game.toStage and game.fromStage convert between play's units and the stage, which differ by where the design is under fit: 'expand', as in a mini game on a tall phone.
play's game.text takes vertical: true or { column }: top to bottom, columns from right to left, marks in their upright forms. A paragraph does not lay out vertical text yet.
An asset manager keeps one paragraph cache and one text cache for its life, by design; the refusal of a second now says to keep the first and pass it wherever a cache is asked for.
Content builds keep Node 26.7.0 exactly, since the producer's versions are part of every build key and compressed images depend on Node's zlib; the refusal names the Node found and why.
A World3D loop stopped and started again re-anchors its clock, so the first frame after a long stop no longer throws CLOCK_DELTA_LIMIT.
Images wholly clipped away, such as labels scrolled out of a clipped panel, no longer count against a shared frame's page budget.
A save store's update changes a copy, which becomes the data only once it passes validate: a refused or throwing change leaves the save in memory as it was.
A managed UI root can be made from a button's callback, while input is being delivered.
A sideways scroll list reads an ordinary vertical mouse wheel.
What a save store's update callback returns, other than undefined, replaces the data only if it passes validate; write a change as a block. shapeOf gives the validate.

createActionControl takes activation: 'releaseInside', which activates only when the captured contact ends inside the target's authored hitArea, or 'tap', which also needs the press to stay within tapTolerance. capturedRelease stays the documented default, so holds keep their contact.

Toggles and selection groups take activation and tapTolerance too, and hand them to the press of the switch or of each item: with 'releaseInside' a press released off its target neither flips a toggle nor selects an item. Keys, movement and scripted calls are unchanged.
